events.title: Giotto completes the Arena Chapel fresco cycle
events.titleZh: 乔托完成斯克罗威尼礼拜堂湿壁画
events.summary: Giotto's Arena Chapel cycle gave Christian narrative painting a new sense of bodily weight, emotional staging, and coherent pictorial space.
events.summaryZh: 乔托的斯克罗威尼礼拜堂壁画让基督教叙事绘画获得新的身体重量、情感场景和连贯图像空间。
events.eventIntro: Around 1305, Giotto completed the frescoes of the Arena Chapel in Padua. The cycle did not simply decorate a chapel; it reorganized biblical storytelling through sequential scenes, embodied figures, architectural settings, and viewer movement through the room.
events.eventIntroZh: 约 1305 年，乔托完成帕多瓦斯克罗威尼礼拜堂的湿壁画。它不只是装饰礼拜堂，而是通过连续场景、具身体感的人物、建筑空间和观者在室内的移动，重新组织圣经叙事。
events.whyMatters: The chapel became a turning point for Western painting because it made sacred narrative feel spatially and emotionally present. Later Renaissance artists could build on Giotto's experiments with volume, gesture, and visual drama.
events.whyMattersZh: 这座礼拜堂成为西方绘画转折点，因为它让神圣叙事具有空间和情感上的临场感。后来的文艺复兴艺术家得以在乔托对体积、手势和视觉戏剧性的实验上继续发展。
events.phaseRelation: This belongs to the Icon, fresco, and devotional painting phase: it shows religious painting moving from symbolic image toward immersive, narrative sacred space.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“圣像、湿壁画与宗教绘画”阶段：它显示宗教绘画从象征图像走向沉浸式、叙事性的神圣空间。
events.connectionHint: It connects naturally to Renaissance perspective, church patronage, and the later idea that painting could guide a viewer through a constructed world.
events.connectionHintZh: 它自然连接到文艺复兴透视法、教会赞助，以及后来绘画可以引导观者进入建构世界的观念。
sourceNotes: The Arena Chapel fresco cycle is commonly dated to about 1303-1305 and treated as a key moment in late medieval and proto-Renaissance painting.
events.imageAlt: Giotto's Lamentation fresco in the Arena Chapel.
events.imageCaption: The Lamentation shows Giotto's use of gesture, mass, and emotional staging inside the Arena Chapel cycle.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《哀悼基督》展示了乔托在斯克罗威尼礼拜堂组画中对手势、体量和情感场景的运用。

events.title: Jan van Eyck paints the Arnolfini Portrait
events.titleZh: 扬·范艾克绘制《阿尔诺芬尼夫妇像》
events.summary: The Arnolfini Portrait made oil painting a vehicle for domestic space, material detail, social status, and visual ambiguity.
events.summaryZh: 《阿尔诺芬尼夫妇像》让油画成为表现家庭空间、物质细节、社会身份和视觉暧昧性的媒介。
events.eventIntro: In 1434, Jan van Eyck painted a double portrait filled with reflective surfaces, textiles, gestures, inscriptions, and carefully observed objects. The painting uses oil technique to make social life appear materially dense and symbolically charged.
events.eventIntroZh: 1434 年，扬·范艾克绘制了一幅充满反射表面、织物、手势、题记和细致物件的双人肖像。它利用油画技术，让社会生活显得物质密集并带有象征意味。
events.whyMatters: The work became a touchstone for Northern Renaissance painting because it showed how oil could render light, texture, identity, and domestic setting with unusual precision.
events.whyMattersZh: 这件作品成为北方文艺复兴绘画的关键案例，因为它展示油画如何以异常精细的方式表现光、质地、身份和家庭空间。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to the Renaissance perspective and oil painting phase, but it represents a northern path: not only geometry and antiquity, but surface, object, contract, and domestic realism.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“文艺复兴透视与油画”阶段，但代表的是北方路径：不仅是几何和古典复兴，也包括表面、物件、契约和家庭现实感。
events.connectionHint: It connects to later portraiture, merchant culture, marriage imagery, and the rise of painting as a medium for recording private status.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到后来的肖像画、商人文化、婚姻图像，以及绘画作为记录私人身份媒介的兴起。
sourceNotes: The National Gallery identifies the painting as Jan van Eyck's 1434 portrait, a canonical Northern Renaissance work.
events.imageCaption: The Arnolfini Portrait uses oil technique to make domestic space, clothing, light, and status unusually legible.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《阿尔诺芬尼夫妇像》用油画技术让家庭空间、服饰、光线和身份异常清晰可见。

events.title: Leonardo completes The Last Supper
events.titleZh: 列奥纳多完成《最后的晚餐》
events.summary: Leonardo's Last Supper turned a monastic dining wall into a psychological and spatial drama of recognition, betrayal, and sacred presence.
events.summaryZh: 列奥纳多的《最后的晚餐》把修道院餐厅墙面变成关于认知、背叛与神圣临场的心理和空间戏剧。
events.eventIntro: By 1498, Leonardo da Vinci had completed The Last Supper for Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan. The composition organizes the apostles' reactions around Christ with architectural perspective, controlled gesture, and a charged narrative instant.
events.eventIntroZh: 到 1498 年，列奥纳多·达·芬奇为米兰圣玛利亚感恩教堂完成《最后的晚餐》。画面用建筑透视、克制手势和高度紧张的叙事瞬间，把使徒围绕基督的反应组织起来。
events.whyMatters: The work became one of the clearest demonstrations of Renaissance painting as a system for arranging bodies, space, emotion, theology, and viewer attention.
events.whyMattersZh: 这件作品成为文艺复兴绘画最清楚的示范之一：绘画可以成为组织身体、空间、情感、神学和观者注意力的系统。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Renaissance perspective and oil painting because it makes spatial construction and human psychology central to devotional image-making.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“文艺复兴透视与油画”阶段，因为它把空间建构和人的心理反应放到宗教图像制作的中心。
events.connectionHint: It connects to architecture, monastic practice, patronage by Milanese rulers, and later debates over conservation and the fragility of experimental technique.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到建筑、修道院实践、米兰统治者赞助，以及后来围绕保护和实验技法脆弱性的争论。
sourceNotes: The Last Supper is usually dated to Leonardo's Milan period, completed in the late 1490s.
events.imageAlt: Leonardo da Vinci's The Last Supper.
events.imageCaption: The Last Supper uses perspective and gesture to turn a biblical meal into a psychological scene.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《最后的晚餐》用透视和手势把圣经中的一餐转化为心理场景。

events.title: Raphael completes The School of Athens
events.titleZh: 拉斐尔完成《雅典学院》
events.summary: Raphael's fresco staged classical philosophy as a Renaissance architecture of knowledge, perspective, and humanist memory.
events.summaryZh: 拉斐尔的壁画把古典哲学表现为由知识、透视和人文主义记忆构成的文艺复兴建筑。
events.eventIntro: Around 1511, Raphael completed The School of Athens in the Vatican Stanze. The fresco imagines ancient philosophers gathered inside an ideal architectural space, turning learning itself into a visual order.
events.eventIntroZh: 约 1511 年，拉斐尔在梵蒂冈签字厅完成《雅典学院》。这幅壁画想象古代哲学家聚集在理想建筑空间中，把学习本身转化为视觉秩序。
events.whyMatters: The painting became a canonical expression of High Renaissance humanism: classical antiquity, mathematical space, papal patronage, and artistic self-consciousness all meet in one image.
events.whyMattersZh: 这幅画成为盛期文艺复兴人文主义的经典表达：古典传统、数学空间、教皇赞助和艺术自觉在同一图像中汇合。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Renaissance perspective and oil painting because it shows perspective not as a trick, but as a worldview for organizing knowledge and authority.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“文艺复兴透视与油画”阶段，因为它显示透视并非单纯技巧，而是组织知识和权威的世界观。
events.connectionHint: It connects art to philosophy, education, church power, and the later museum idea of Renaissance art as a high point of European culture.
events.connectionHintZh: 它把艺术连接到哲学、教育、教会权力，以及后来把文艺复兴艺术视为欧洲文化高峰的博物馆叙事。
sourceNotes: The School of Athens is a central Vatican Stanze fresco associated with Raphael's mature Roman work.
events.imageCaption: The School of Athens visualizes Renaissance humanism through classical figures inside an ideal architectural space.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《雅典学院》通过理想建筑空间中的古典人物，把文艺复兴人文主义视觉化。

events.title: Velazquez paints Las Meninas
events.titleZh: 委拉斯开兹绘制《宫娥》
events.summary: Las Meninas made court painting a meditation on spectatorship, royal power, artistic labor, and the unstable position of the viewer.
events.summaryZh: 《宫娥》让宫廷绘画成为关于观看、王权、艺术劳动和观者位置不稳定性的思考。
events.eventIntro: In 1656, Diego Velazquez painted Las Meninas at the Spanish court. The image places the painter, the infanta, attendants, mirror, doorway, and implied royal viewers into a complex spatial and social puzzle.
events.eventIntroZh: 1656 年，迭戈·委拉斯开兹在西班牙宫廷创作《宫娥》。画面把画家、公主、侍女、镜子、门口和被暗示的王室观看者放入复杂的空间与社会谜题中。
events.whyMatters: The painting matters because it turns representation itself into the subject. It shows Baroque court art as both display of hierarchy and subtle inquiry into who sees, who is seen, and who has power.
events.whyMattersZh: 这幅画重要，因为它把“再现”本身变成主题。它显示巴洛克宫廷艺术既展示等级秩序，也细致追问谁在看、谁被看、谁拥有权力。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Baroque, court, and global painting markets because it uses court spectacle and painterly intelligence to expose the mechanics of representation.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“巴洛克、宫廷与全球绘画市场”阶段，因为它用宫廷奇观和绘画智慧揭示再现机制。
events.connectionHint: It connects to monarchy, court ritual, portraiture, later modernist art theory, and museum debates about the viewer's role.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到君主制、宫廷礼仪、肖像画、后来的现代主义艺术理论，以及关于观者角色的博物馆讨论。
sourceNotes: Las Meninas is one of the central works of Spanish Baroque painting and court portraiture.
events.imageCaption: Las Meninas makes court space, artistic labor, and royal spectatorship part of the same visual puzzle.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《宫娥》把宫廷空间、艺术劳动和王室观看共同变成同一个视觉谜题。

events.title: Impression, Sunrise is shown at the first Impressionist exhibition
events.titleZh: 《印象·日出》在首届印象派展览展出
events.summary: Monet's Impression, Sunrise helped name Impressionism and made quick perception, light, atmosphere, and modern exhibition independence central to painting.
events.summaryZh: 莫奈的《印象·日出》帮助命名印象派，并让瞬时感知、光、空气感和现代独立展览成为绘画核心。
events.eventIntro: In 1874, Claude Monet's Impression, Sunrise was shown in the independent exhibition organized by artists outside the official Salon system. A critic's use of the word impression helped give the movement its name.
events.eventIntroZh: 1874 年，克洛德·莫奈的《印象·日出》在艺术家脱离官方沙龙体系组织的独立展览中展出。一位评论家使用“印象”一词，帮助这个运动获得名称。
events.whyMatters: The event matters because it linked a new painterly surface to a new exhibition politics. Impressionism challenged academic finish, official gatekeeping, and older ideas of stable subject matter.
events.whyMattersZh: 这个事件重要，因为它把新的绘画表面与新的展览政治连接起来。印象派挑战学院式完成度、官方把关机制和旧有稳定题材观。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Modern painting and abstraction because it shifted painting toward perception, modern life, and the visible facture of paint.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“现代绘画与抽象”阶段，因为它把绘画推向感知、现代生活和可见的绘画笔触。
events.connectionHint: It connects to photography, railways, leisure, urban modernity, art markets, and the broader move from academic institutions to independent avant-gardes.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到摄影、铁路、休闲、都市现代性、艺术市场，以及从学院制度转向独立先锋的更广泛变化。
sourceNotes: The 1874 independent exhibition and Monet's painting are canonical in histories of Impressionism.
events.imageCaption: Impression, Sunrise made atmospheric perception and independent exhibition culture part of modern painting's story.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《印象·日出》让空气感知和独立展览文化成为现代绘画故事的一部分。

events.title: Duchamp submits Fountain
events.titleZh: 杜尚提交《泉》
events.summary: Duchamp's Fountain turned selection, context, authorship, and institutional framing into central questions for modern art.
events.summaryZh: 杜尚的《泉》把选择、语境、作者身份和制度框架变成现代艺术的核心问题。
events.eventIntro: In 1917, Marcel Duchamp submitted a signed urinal titled Fountain to the Society of Independent Artists in New York. Its rejection exposed the limits of supposedly open exhibition rules and made the readymade a provocation.
events.eventIntroZh: 1917 年，马塞尔·杜尚向纽约独立艺术家协会提交了一个署名为《泉》的小便池。它被拒绝，暴露出所谓开放展览规则的边界，也让现成品成为挑衅。
events.whyMatters: Fountain mattered because it shifted attention from hand-made form to decision, naming, display, and institutional authority. It changed what later artists could ask an artwork to be.
events.whyMattersZh: 《泉》重要，因为它把注意力从手工形式转向决定、命名、展示和制度权威。它改变了后来艺术家对“艺术品可以是什么”的提问方式。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Modern painting and abstraction broadly because the modernist break included not only abstraction, but also attacks on medium, authorship, and taste.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它广义上属于“现代绘画与抽象”阶段，因为现代主义断裂不仅包括抽象，也包括对媒介、作者身份和品味的攻击。
events.connectionHint: It connects to conceptual art, museum critique, design objects, commodity culture, and later digital debates over originality and reproducibility.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到观念艺术、博物馆批判、设计物品、商品文化，以及后来数字时代关于原创性和可复制性的争论。
sourceNotes: Fountain is a canonical readymade and foundational case for twentieth-century conceptual art.
events.imageAlt: Alfred Stieglitz photograph of Marcel Duchamp's Fountain.
events.imageCaption: Stieglitz's photograph is central because the original Fountain was lost; the image helped preserve the provocation.
events.imageCaptionZh: 施蒂格利茨的照片很关键，因为《泉》的原件已遗失；这张照片帮助保存了这次挑衅。

events.title: Malevich exhibits Black Square
events.titleZh: 马列维奇展出《黑方块》
events.summary: Black Square made abstraction appear as a radical zero point, rejecting representational painting for a new pictorial and philosophical language.
events.summaryZh: 《黑方块》让抽象成为激进的零点，拒绝再现绘画，提出新的图像与哲学语言。
events.eventIntro: In 1915, Kazimir Malevich exhibited Black Square in Petrograd at The Last Futurist Exhibition of Paintings 0,10. Hung high in a corner, it echoed the position of an icon while refusing recognizable religious or natural imagery.
events.eventIntroZh: 1915 年，卡济米尔·马列维奇在彼得格勒“最后的未来主义绘画展 0,10”中展出《黑方块》。它被高挂在角落，呼应圣像位置，却拒绝任何可识别的宗教或自然图像。
events.whyMatters: The painting mattered because it made abstraction a total program rather than a stylistic variation. It asked viewers to treat surface, geometry, and idea as sufficient artistic content.
events.whyMattersZh: 这幅画重要，因为它把抽象变成完整纲领，而不只是风格变化。它要求观者把表面、几何和观念本身视为足够的艺术内容。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Modern painting and abstraction because it shows painting breaking from depiction into systems of form, ideology, and avant-garde manifesto.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“现代绘画与抽象”阶段，因为它显示绘画从描绘转向形式系统、意识形态和先锋宣言。
events.connectionHint: It connects to Russian avant-garde politics, design, constructivism, minimalism, and later debates about whether an artwork can begin from almost nothing.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到俄罗斯先锋政治、设计、构成主义、极简主义，以及后来关于艺术品是否可以从近乎空无开始的争论。
sourceNotes: Black Square and the 0,10 exhibition are central in accounts of Suprematism and the Russian avant-garde.
events.imageCaption: Black Square made the rejection of depiction into a concentrated modernist statement.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《黑方块》把对描绘的拒绝凝缩为现代主义宣言。

events.title: Warhol exhibits Campbell's Soup Cans
events.titleZh: 沃霍尔展出《金宝汤罐头》
events.summary: Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans made supermarket packaging, repetition, advertising, and art-world display part of the same visual economy.
events.summaryZh: 沃霍尔的《金宝汤罐头》把超市包装、重复、广告和艺术展览纳入同一个视觉经济。
events.eventIntro: In 1962, Andy Warhol exhibited Campbell's Soup Cans in Los Angeles. The work presented familiar commercial packaging as serial painted panels, flattening the distance between consumer culture and fine art.
events.eventIntroZh: 1962 年，安迪·沃霍尔在洛杉矶展出《金宝汤罐头》。作品把熟悉的商业包装作为连续绘画面板呈现，压缩了消费文化与高级艺术之间的距离。
events.whyMatters: The exhibition mattered because it made Pop Art's argument visible: modern images were already industrial, branded, repeated, and consumed before they entered the gallery.
events.whyMattersZh: 这次展览重要，因为它让波普艺术的论点变得可见：现代图像在进入画廊之前，就已经是工业化、品牌化、重复和被消费的。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Contemporary global visual art because it points toward a world where painting, media, commodity design, celebrity, and markets constantly overlap.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“当代全球视觉艺术”阶段，因为它指向绘画、媒体、商品设计、名人和市场不断重叠的世界。
events.connectionHint: It connects to advertising, television, supermarkets, celebrity culture, and later debates about appropriation and image saturation.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到广告、电视、超市、名人文化，以及后来关于挪用和图像过剩的讨论。
sourceNotes: Campbell's Soup Cans is a central early Pop Art exhibition work by Andy Warhol.
events.imageAlt: Andy Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans installed at MoMA.
events.imageCaption: Campbell's Soup Cans turns branded repetition into a subject for painting and museum display.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《金宝汤罐头》把品牌化重复变成绘画和博物馆展示的主题。

events.title: Daguerreotype process announced
events.titleZh: 银版摄影法公布
events.summary: The public announcement of the daguerreotype made photography a practical public technology for fixing images made by light.
events.summaryZh: 银版摄影法的公开宣布，让摄影成为一种用光固定图像的实际公共技术。
events.eventIntro: In 1839, the French state announced Louis Daguerre's photographic process to the public. The daguerreotype produced detailed images on silvered plates and quickly drew scientific, artistic, commercial, and popular attention.
events.eventIntroZh: 1839 年，法国政府向公众公布路易·达盖尔的摄影方法。银版摄影能在镀银板上生成细节丰富的图像，很快吸引科学、艺术、商业和大众兴趣。
events.whyMatters: The announcement matters because it made photography a public medium almost immediately. Portrait studios, scientific documentation, urban views, colonial records, and family memory all changed around chemical images.
events.whyMattersZh: 这次公布重要，因为它几乎立刻让摄影成为公共媒介。肖像馆、科学记录、城市景观、殖民档案和家庭记忆都围绕化学图像发生变化。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Daguerreotype and early photographic studios because it marks photography's transition from experiment to public practice.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“银版摄影与早期照相馆”阶段，因为它标志摄影从实验转向公共实践。
events.connectionHint: It connects to industrial chemistry, portrait commerce, state patronage, visual evidence, and later arguments over whether photography was art or technology.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到工业化学、肖像商业、国家赞助、视觉证据，以及后来关于摄影是艺术还是技术的争论。
sourceNotes: 1839 is conventionally treated as photography's public birth year through the daguerreotype announcement.
events.imageCaption: Daguerre's Boulevard du Temple shows the kind of chemically fixed urban image that made the new medium startling.
events.imageCaptionZh: 达盖尔的《坦普尔大道》展示了这种化学固定城市图像为何令人震惊。

events.title: Talbot patents the calotype process
events.titleZh: 塔尔博特获得卡罗式摄影法专利
events.summary: The calotype introduced a negative-positive photographic process that made reproducible paper photographs central to photography's future.
events.summaryZh: 卡罗式摄影法引入负片—正片流程，让可复制的纸基照片成为摄影未来的核心。
events.eventIntro: In 1841, William Henry Fox Talbot patented the calotype in Britain. Unlike a unique daguerreotype plate, the calotype used a paper negative from which multiple positive prints could be made.
events.eventIntroZh: 1841 年，威廉·亨利·福克斯·塔尔博特在英国为卡罗式摄影法申请专利。不同于唯一的银版照片，卡罗式使用纸质负片，可以制作多个正片。
events.whyMatters: The process mattered because it pointed photography toward reproducibility, albums, archives, publishing, and later film-based image culture.
events.whyMattersZh: 这一方法重要，因为它把摄影推向可复制性、相册、档案、出版以及后来的胶片图像文化。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to the Daguerreotype and early photographic studios phase, but it represents a different future: photography as repeatable paper image rather than singular metal plate.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“银版摄影与早期照相馆”阶段，但代表另一种未来：摄影作为可重复的纸上图像，而不是唯一金属板。
events.connectionHint: It connects to books, archives, illustrated journalism, family albums, and the later technical logic of negatives and prints.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到书籍、档案、图像新闻、家庭相册，以及后来负片和照片冲印的技术逻辑。
sourceNotes: Talbot's calotype patent is central in histories of photographic reproducibility.
events.imageAlt: William Henry Fox Talbot's The Open Door.
events.imageCaption: Talbot's paper photographs show how the calotype tied photography to reproducible prints rather than single plates.
events.imageCaptionZh: 塔尔博特的纸基照片显示卡罗式摄影如何把摄影连接到可复制照片，而不是单一金属板。

events.title: Antietam photographs exhibited in New York
events.titleZh: 安提坦战场照片在纽约展出
events.summary: The exhibition of Civil War battlefield photographs brought the visual evidence of dead soldiers into urban public view.
events.summaryZh: 美国内战战场照片展出，把阵亡士兵的视觉证据带入城市公共视野。
events.eventIntro: In 1862, photographs of the dead at Antietam, taken by Alexander Gardner and associated with Mathew Brady's gallery, were exhibited in New York. Viewers encountered war through photographic evidence rather than heroic painting alone.
events.eventIntroZh: 1862 年，亚历山大·加德纳拍摄、与马修·布雷迪画廊相关的安提坦阵亡者照片在纽约展出。观众不再只通过英雄化绘画理解战争，而是面对摄影证据。
events.whyMatters: The event mattered because it changed the public relationship to war images. Photography could make distant violence look factual, immediate, and morally uncomfortable.
events.whyMattersZh: 这个事件重要，因为它改变了公众与战争图像的关系。摄影能让遥远暴力显得真实、即时并带来道德不安。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Documentary, portrait, and colonial photography because it shows photography entering war reporting, evidence, memory, and public display.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“纪实、肖像与殖民摄影”阶段，因为它显示摄影进入战争报道、证据、记忆和公共展示。
events.connectionHint: It connects to photojournalism, military history, public mourning, propaganda, and later debates over whether graphic images should be shown.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到新闻摄影、军事史、公共哀悼、宣传，以及后来关于是否应展示惨烈图像的争论。
sourceNotes: Civil War battlefield photography, especially Antietam, is widely treated as a turning point in war imagery.
events.imageAlt: Dead Confederate soldiers photographed after the Battle of Antietam.
events.imageCaption: Antietam photographs confronted viewers with the dead of war as visual evidence rather than heroic allegory.
events.imageCaptionZh: 安提坦照片让观众面对作为视觉证据的战争死者，而不是英雄寓言。
events.imageCredit: Image: Library of Congress / Wikimedia Commons

events.title: Kodak camera is launched
events.titleZh: 柯达相机上市
events.summary: The Kodak camera made photography easier for amateurs and turned picture-making into a consumer service system.
events.summaryZh: 柯达相机降低了业余摄影门槛，把拍照变成一种消费服务系统。
events.eventIntro: In 1888, George Eastman's Kodak camera reached consumers with the promise that users could press the button while Kodak handled the rest. The camera, film, processing, and prints became a linked service.
events.eventIntroZh: 1888 年，乔治·伊士曼的柯达相机面向消费者推出，承诺用户只需按下按钮，其余交给柯达。相机、胶片、冲洗和照片成为一套连接服务。
events.whyMatters: The launch mattered because photography moved from a specialist craft toward everyday amateur practice. Family memory, tourism, leisure, and consumer branding all changed with portable cameras.
events.whyMattersZh: 这次上市重要，因为摄影从专业技艺走向日常业余实践。家庭记忆、旅行、休闲和消费品牌都随着便携相机发生变化。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Documentary, portrait, and colonial photography because it widened who could make images and how photographs circulated socially.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“纪实、肖像与殖民摄影”阶段，因为它扩大了谁能制作图像以及照片如何在社会中流通。
events.connectionHint: It connects to advertising, family albums, tourism, mass manufacturing, and later smartphone photography as a consumer image habit.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到广告、家庭相册、旅游、大规模制造，以及后来智能手机摄影作为消费图像习惯的形成。
sourceNotes: The 1888 Kodak camera is a standard milestone in consumer photography.
events.imageAlt: Advertisement for the Kodak camera from the late 1880s.
events.imageCaption: Kodak advertising framed photography as a consumer service: press the button, let the company do the rest.
events.imageCaptionZh: 柯达广告把摄影塑造成消费服务：按下按钮，剩下交给公司。

events.title: Leica I camera is introduced
events.titleZh: 徕卡 I 型相机推出
events.summary: The Leica I helped make 35mm photography compact, mobile, and central to modernist and documentary visual culture.
events.summaryZh: 徕卡 I 型推动 35mm 摄影变得小型、机动，并成为现代主义与纪实视觉文化的重要工具。
events.eventIntro: In 1925, the Leica I was introduced commercially. Its compact 35mm format let photographers move differently through streets, events, and everyday life than bulky plate cameras had allowed.
events.eventIntroZh: 1925 年，徕卡 I 型正式商业推出。它的小型 35mm 格式让摄影师能以不同于笨重板式相机的方式穿行街道、事件和日常生活。
events.whyMatters: The camera mattered because it helped create a mobile photographic eye. Modernist composition, street photography, war reporting, and illustrated magazines all benefited from smaller cameras.
events.whyMattersZh: 这台相机重要，因为它帮助形成机动摄影之眼。现代主义构图、街头摄影、战争报道和图像杂志都受益于小型相机。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Modernist photography and mass magazines because camera portability changed both what could be photographed and how images could feed mass visual culture.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“现代主义摄影与大众杂志”阶段，因为相机便携性改变了可拍摄对象，也改变了图像进入大众视觉文化的方式。
events.connectionHint: It connects to photojournalism, urban modernity, design engineering, and later portable media devices.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到新闻摄影、都市现代性、设计工程，以及后来各种便携媒体设备。
sourceNotes: The Leica I is a standard milestone in 35mm photography and modern camera design.
events.imageCaption: The Leica I made small-format photography a practical tool for mobile modern image-making.
events.imageCaptionZh: 徕卡 I 型让小画幅摄影成为机动现代图像制作的实际工具。

events.title: Farm Security Administration photography project begins
events.titleZh: 美国农业安全局摄影项目启动
events.summary: The FSA photography project made documentary images part of New Deal public communication and the visual memory of the Great Depression.
events.summaryZh: 美国农业安全局摄影项目让纪实图像成为新政公共传播和大萧条视觉记忆的一部分。
events.eventIntro: In 1935, the U.S. government's resettlement and farm programs began building what became the Farm Security Administration photography project. Photographers documented rural poverty, migration, labor, and social change.
events.eventIntroZh: 1935 年，美国政府的移民安置与农业项目开始形成后来被称为农业安全局的摄影计划。摄影师记录农村贫困、迁徙、劳动和社会变化。
events.whyMatters: The project mattered because it made state-sponsored photography a tool of evidence, persuasion, reform, and national memory. Its images shaped how Americans imagined the Depression.
events.whyMattersZh: 这个项目重要，因为它让国家资助的摄影成为证据、说服、改革和国家记忆的工具。其图像塑造了美国人对大萧条的想象。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Modernist photography and mass magazines because documentary style, public policy, and mass circulation became deeply connected.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“现代主义摄影与大众杂志”阶段，因为纪实风格、公共政策和大众传播在此深度连接。
events.connectionHint: It connects to welfare-state politics, documentary film, photojournalism, archives, and debates about representation of poverty.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到福利国家政治、纪录片、新闻摄影、档案，以及关于贫困再现的争论。
sourceNotes: The FSA photographic archive is a major public collection and documentary photography milestone.
events.imageCaption: Migrant Mother became one of the most recognized images associated with FSA documentary photography.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《移民母亲》成为与农业安全局纪实摄影相关的最著名图像之一。
events.imageCredit: Image: Library of Congress / Wikimedia Commons

events.title: Polaroid Land Camera is demonstrated
events.titleZh: 宝丽来 Land 相机公开演示
events.summary: Polaroid's instant camera made photographic time collapse from delayed processing into immediate viewing and sharing.
events.summaryZh: 宝丽来即时相机把摄影时间从延迟冲洗压缩为即时观看与分享。
events.eventIntro: In 1947, Edwin Land demonstrated the Polaroid Land Camera, an instant photographic system that produced a developed print shortly after exposure. It turned waiting for photographs into part of the problem the camera solved.
events.eventIntroZh: 1947 年，埃德温·兰德公开演示宝丽来 Land 相机，这是一套能在曝光后很快产生成像照片的即时摄影系统。它把等待照片这件事变成相机要解决的问题。
events.whyMatters: Instant photography changed the social rhythm of image-making. Pictures could be checked, exchanged, and performed in the moment, linking photography to play, intimacy, documentation, and consumer novelty.
events.whyMattersZh: 即时摄影改变了图像制作的社会节奏。照片可以当场检查、交换和表演，把摄影连接到游戏、亲密关系、记录和消费新奇感。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Photojournalism, advertising, and art photography because postwar photography increasingly moved through consumer devices, design, and mass-market image habits.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“新闻摄影、广告与艺术摄影”阶段，因为战后摄影越来越通过消费设备、设计和大众图像习惯运作。
events.connectionHint: It connects to family snapshots, advertising, identity photos, artists' instant-image experiments, and later smartphone expectations of immediate feedback.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到家庭快照、广告、证件照、艺术家的即时图像实验，以及后来智能手机对即时反馈的期待。
sourceNotes: The public demonstration of instant photography is a standard Polaroid milestone.
events.imageCaption: The Land Camera made instant photographic feedback a consumer experience.
events.imageCaptionZh: Land 相机把即时摄影反馈变成消费体验。

events.title: Kodak DCS 100 digital camera system released
events.titleZh: 柯达 DCS 100 数码相机系统发布
events.summary: The Kodak DCS 100 made professional digital photography commercially available, linking cameras, sensors, storage, and computer workflows.
events.summaryZh: 柯达 DCS 100 让专业数码摄影进入商业可用阶段，把相机、传感器、存储和计算机流程连接起来。
events.eventIntro: In 1991, Kodak released the DCS 100, a professional digital camera system built around a modified Nikon body and an external storage unit. It was expensive and specialized, but it made digital capture a real working tool.
events.eventIntroZh: 1991 年，柯达发布 DCS 100 专业数码相机系统，基于改装尼康机身和外置存储单元。它昂贵且专门化，但让数码捕捉成为真实工作工具。
events.whyMatters: The DCS 100 mattered because it moved photography toward sensor data, files, storage, and software. It foreshadowed the digital workflow that would later transform journalism, archives, editing, and everyday image culture.
events.whyMattersZh: DCS 100 重要，因为它把摄影推向传感器数据、文件、存储和软件。它预示了后来改变新闻、档案、编辑和日常图像文化的数字流程。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Digital photography and networked images because it marks the professional transition from chemical film to digital capture.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“数字摄影与网络图像”阶段，因为它标志专业摄影从化学胶片转向数字捕捉。
events.connectionHint: It connects to CCD sensors, Photoshop, newsroom digitization, databases, and the later smartphone camera ecosystem.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到 CCD 传感器、Photoshop、新闻编辑部数字化、数据库，以及后来的智能手机相机生态。
sourceNotes: The Kodak DCS line is widely cited in histories of professional digital photography.
events.imageCaption: The DCS 100 shows early digital photography as a hybrid of camera body, sensor, storage, and computer workflow.
events.imageCaptionZh: DCS 100 显示早期数码摄影是相机机身、传感器、存储和计算机流程的混合体。

events.title: Adobe Photoshop 1.0 is released
events.titleZh: Adobe Photoshop 1.0 发布
events.summary: Photoshop made digital image manipulation a practical tool for designers, photographers, publishers, artists, and later everyday visual culture.
events.summaryZh: Photoshop 让数字图像处理成为设计师、摄影师、出版者、艺术家以及后来日常视觉文化的实际工具。
events.eventIntro: In 1990, Adobe released Photoshop 1.0 for the Macintosh. The software gave desktop users a practical environment for editing, compositing, retouching, and transforming raster images.
events.eventIntroZh: 1990 年，Adobe 为 Macintosh 发布 Photoshop 1.0。这款软件为桌面用户提供了编辑、合成、修饰和转换位图图像的实际环境。
events.whyMatters: Photoshop mattered because it normalized the idea that photographs and images were editable data. It changed publishing, advertising, art, journalism, and public trust in photographic evidence.
events.whyMattersZh: Photoshop 重要，因为它让照片和图像是可编辑数据这一观念常态化。它改变了出版、广告、艺术、新闻以及公众对摄影证据的信任。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Digital photography and networked images, and also to digital/new media art, because image editing became part of the basic grammar of digital culture.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“数字摄影与网络图像”，也属于数字/新媒体艺术，因为图像编辑成为数字文化的基本语法之一。
events.connectionHint: It connects to desktop publishing, web images, memes, visual misinformation, and AI image tools that later automated parts of editing and generation.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到桌面出版、网络图像、模因、视觉误导，以及后来把部分编辑和生成自动化的 AI 图像工具。
sourceNotes: Photoshop 1.0 is a standard milestone in digital imaging and design software history.
events.imageCaption: Photoshop became the shorthand for digital image editing, even as the software evolved far beyond its first release.
events.imageCaptionZh: Photoshop 成为数字图像编辑的代名词，即使软件本身早已远远超出最初版本。

events.title: Cybernetic Serendipity opens in London
events.titleZh: 《控制论偶然性》展览在伦敦开幕
events.summary: Cybernetic Serendipity brought computers, cybernetics, art, music, machines, and interactive systems into a major public exhibition.
events.summaryZh: 《控制论偶然性》把计算机、控制论、艺术、音乐、机器和互动系统带入大型公共展览。
events.eventIntro: In 1968, the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London opened Cybernetic Serendipity, curated by Jasia Reichardt. The exhibition gathered artists, engineers, composers, machines, and computer-generated works.
events.eventIntroZh: 1968 年，伦敦当代艺术学院开幕由雅西亚·赖夏特策划的《控制论偶然性》。展览汇集艺术家、工程师、作曲家、机器和计算机生成作品。
events.whyMatters: The exhibition mattered because it made computer art visible as a cultural field rather than a technical curiosity. It also showed that computation could be playful, participatory, sonic, visual, and institutional.
events.whyMattersZh: 这次展览重要，因为它让计算机艺术作为文化领域可见，而不只是技术奇观。它也显示计算可以是游戏性的、参与性的、声音的、视觉的和制度性的。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Computer art and algorithmic graphics because it staged algorithmic and cybernetic practices for a broad art audience.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“计算机艺术与算法图形”阶段，因为它把算法和控制论实践展示给更广泛的艺术观众。
events.connectionHint: It connects to software, systems theory, experimental music, interaction design, and later digital art festivals.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到软件、系统理论、实验音乐、交互设计以及后来的数字艺术节。
sourceNotes: Cybernetic Serendipity is a canonical exhibition in histories of computer art and cybernetic art.
events.imageAlt: Catalogue cover for the Cybernetic Serendipity exhibition.
events.imageCaption: The Cybernetic Serendipity catalogue became a visual record of early computer and cybernetic art entering public culture.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《控制论偶然性》展览图录成为早期计算机与控制论艺术进入公共文化的视觉记录。

events.title: Experiments in Art and Technology is founded
events.titleZh: “艺术与技术实验”组织成立
events.summary: Experiments in Art and Technology connected artists and engineers, making collaboration itself a model for new media practice.
events.summaryZh: “艺术与技术实验”组织连接艺术家和工程师，让协作本身成为新媒体实践的模式。
events.eventIntro: In 1966, artists and engineers associated with 9 Evenings helped form Experiments in Art and Technology in New York. E.A.T. treated electronics, performance, engineering, and organizational matchmaking as part of artistic production.
events.eventIntroZh: 1966 年，与《九个夜晚》相关的艺术家和工程师在纽约推动成立“艺术与技术实验”组织。E.A.T. 把电子技术、表演、工程和组织配对都视为艺术生产的一部分。
events.whyMatters: The organization mattered because it built a social infrastructure for art-and-technology collaboration. It showed that new media art depended not only on devices, but also on networks of expertise.
events.whyMattersZh: 这个组织重要，因为它为艺术与技术协作建立了社会基础设施。它显示新媒体艺术不仅依赖设备，也依赖专业知识网络。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Film, video, and electronic image experiments because artists were learning to work with electronics, performance systems, and engineers before personal computers became common.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“电影、视频与电子图像实验”阶段，因为艺术家在个人电脑普及前，就开始与电子设备、表演系统和工程师合作。
events.connectionHint: It connects to performance art, telecommunications art, interactive installation, and later artist-engineer collaborations in software and labs.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到表演艺术、电信艺术、互动装置，以及后来软件和实验室中的艺术家—工程师协作。
sourceNotes: E.A.T. is widely cited as a key organization in art-and-technology collaboration.
events.imageAlt: Poster for 9 Evenings: Theatre and Engineering.
events.imageCaption: 9 Evenings helped create the collaborative environment from which Experiments in Art and Technology emerged.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《九个夜晚》帮助形成“艺术与技术实验”组织出现的协作环境。

events.title: Nam June Paik creates TV Buddha
events.titleZh: 白南准创作《电视佛》
events.summary: TV Buddha staged a sculptural feedback loop between spiritual image, television technology, surveillance, and self-observation.
events.summaryZh: 《电视佛》在精神图像、电视技术、监控与自我观看之间搭建了雕塑式反馈回路。
events.eventIntro: In 1974, Nam June Paik created TV Buddha, placing a Buddha statue before a closed-circuit television image of itself. The work turns television into a loop of meditation, media, and self-reflection.
events.eventIntroZh: 1974 年，白南准创作《电视佛》，把佛像放在显示其自身闭路电视影像的屏幕前。作品把电视转化为冥想、媒介和自我反观的循环。
events.whyMatters: The work mattered because it showed video art could be more than recorded moving image. It could be installation, sculpture, philosophy, technology critique, and cultural translation at once.
events.whyMattersZh: 这件作品重要，因为它显示视频艺术不只是录制的活动图像。它可以同时是装置、雕塑、哲学、技术批判和文化转译。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Video art, installation, and media critique because it uses live video feedback to question television's authority and the viewer's position.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“视频艺术、装置与媒介批判”阶段，因为它用实时视频反馈质疑电视权威和观者位置。
events.connectionHint: It connects to Buddhism, television culture, surveillance, closed-circuit systems, installation art, and later webcam and livestream cultures.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到佛教、电视文化、监控、闭路系统、装置艺术，以及后来的网络摄像头和直播文化。
sourceNotes: TV Buddha is a canonical work in histories of video art and media installation.
events.imageAlt: Nam June Paik's TV Buddha installation.
events.imageCaption: TV Buddha uses closed-circuit television to make a statue watch its own mediated image.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《电视佛》用闭路电视让佛像观看自身的媒介化图像。

events.title: Ars Electronica festival is founded
events.titleZh: 林茨电子艺术节创立
events.summary: Ars Electronica gave electronic and digital art a recurring public festival platform connecting artists, technologists, theorists, and audiences.
events.summaryZh: 林茨电子艺术节为电子与数字艺术提供持续公共平台，连接艺术家、技术人员、理论家和观众。
events.eventIntro: In 1979, Ars Electronica began in Linz, Austria, as a festival for art, technology, and society. It became a recurring site where electronic music, computer graphics, robotics, networks, and media theory could meet.
events.eventIntroZh: 1979 年，林茨电子艺术节在奥地利林茨启动，定位于艺术、技术与社会。它成为电子音乐、计算机图形、机器人、网络和媒介理论持续相遇的场所。
events.whyMatters: The festival mattered because digital art needed institutions as much as machines. Ars Electronica helped create an international public language for media art before the web made digital culture ordinary.
events.whyMattersZh: 这个艺术节重要，因为数字艺术既需要机器，也需要制度。林茨电子艺术节在网络让数字文化日常化之前，就帮助形成了媒体艺术的国际公共语言。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Computer art and algorithmic graphics because it created a durable public platform for computational and electronic practices.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“计算机艺术与算法图形”阶段，因为它为计算和电子实践建立了持久公共平台。
events.connectionHint: It connects to festivals, research labs, creative coding, European media policy, and later AI and interactive art exhibitions.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到艺术节、研究实验室、创意编程、欧洲媒介政策，以及后来的 AI 和互动艺术展览。
sourceNotes: Ars Electronica is a key institution in electronic, digital, and media art history.
events.imageCaption: Ars Electronica became an institutional home for electronic and digital art debates.
events.imageCaptionZh: 林茨电子艺术节成为电子与数字艺术讨论的重要制度场所。

events.title: Rhizome ArtBase begins preserving net art
events.titleZh: Rhizome ArtBase 开始保存网络艺术
events.summary: Rhizome ArtBase helped frame net art as something that needed collection, preservation, metadata, and institutional care.
events.summaryZh: Rhizome ArtBase 帮助把网络艺术理解为需要收藏、保存、元数据和制度照护的对象。
events.eventIntro: In 1999, Rhizome launched ArtBase as an archive for born-digital and internet-based artworks. It treated websites, code, online projects, and networked practices as fragile cultural objects rather than disposable web pages.
events.eventIntroZh: 1999 年，Rhizome 推出 ArtBase，用于存档原生数字和互联网艺术作品。它把网站、代码、在线项目和网络实践视为脆弱文化对象，而不是一次性网页。
events.whyMatters: The project mattered because net art often depended on obsolete browsers, servers, plugins, and social contexts. Preservation became part of the artwork's history, not an afterthought.
events.whyMattersZh: 这个项目重要，因为网络艺术常常依赖过时浏览器、服务器、插件和社会语境。保存成为作品历史的一部分，而不是事后补救。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Internet art and networked participation because it shows the web becoming both artistic medium and archival problem.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“互联网艺术与网络参与”阶段，因为它显示网络既成为艺术媒介，也成为档案难题。
events.connectionHint: It connects to museum conservation, software emulation, platform decay, internet communities, and later blockchain claims about digital ownership.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到博物馆保护、软件模拟、平台衰败、互联网社群，以及后来区块链关于数字所有权的主张。
sourceNotes: Rhizome ArtBase is a central archive for net art and born-digital art preservation.
events.imageCaption: Rhizome became a key institution for treating internet art as preservable cultural work.
events.imageCaptionZh: Rhizome 成为把互联网艺术视为可保存文化作品的重要机构。

events.title: Processing 1.0 is released
events.titleZh: Processing 1.0 发布
events.summary: Processing made creative coding accessible to artists, designers, educators, and students through a visual programming environment.
events.summaryZh: Processing 通过视觉化编程环境，让艺术家、设计师、教育者和学生更容易进入创意编程。
events.eventIntro: In 2008, Processing 1.0 was released after years of development by Casey Reas and Ben Fry. The project offered a language and environment for learning programming through drawing, animation, interaction, and visual systems.
events.eventIntroZh: 2008 年，Casey Reas 和 Ben Fry 开发多年的 Processing 1.0 发布。这个项目提供了一种通过绘图、动画、互动和视觉系统学习编程的语言与环境。
events.whyMatters: Processing mattered because it lowered the threshold for artists and designers to work directly with code. It helped normalize programming as a material for visual culture rather than only an engineering skill.
events.whyMattersZh: Processing 重要，因为它降低了艺术家和设计师直接使用代码的门槛。它帮助把编程常态化为视觉文化材料，而不只是工程技能。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Social media, platforms, and post-internet art only partly; more importantly it bridges interactive multimedia, internet communities, and creative coding education.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它部分属于“社交媒体、平台与后互联网艺术”，但更重要的是连接互动多媒体、互联网社群和创意编程教育。
events.connectionHint: It connects to software education, generative art, data visualization, maker culture, and later p5.js browser-based creative coding.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到软件教育、生成艺术、数据可视化、创客文化，以及后来基于浏览器的 p5.js 创意编程。
sourceNotes: Processing is widely cited in creative coding and digital art education histories.
events.imageCaption: Processing became a recognizable platform for teaching programming as visual and interactive practice.
events.imageCaptionZh: Processing 成为把编程作为视觉和互动实践来教学的标志性平台。

events.title: Beeple's Everydays sells at Christie's
events.titleZh: Beeple《Everydays》在佳士得成交
events.summary: The Christie's sale of Everydays made NFT art a global market spectacle and intensified debates over digital ownership, speculation, and artistic value.
events.summaryZh: 佳士得拍卖 Beeple《Everydays》让 NFT 艺术成为全球市场奇观，并加剧关于数字所有权、投机和艺术价值的争论。
events.eventIntro: In 2021, Beeple's Everydays: The First 5000 Days sold at Christie's as an NFT for a price that shocked both the art world and the crypto world. The event made blockchain-based ownership claims impossible for art institutions to ignore.
events.eventIntroZh: 2021 年，Beeple 的《Everydays: The First 5000 Days》作为 NFT 在佳士得成交，价格震动艺术界和加密圈。这个事件让基于区块链的所有权主张成为艺术机构无法忽视的问题。
events.whyMatters: The sale mattered less because it settled what digital art is, and more because it exposed a collision between markets, platforms, scarcity, authorship, environmental cost, and online communities.
events.whyMattersZh: 这次成交的重要性不在于它解决了数字艺术是什么，而在于它暴露了市场、平台、稀缺性、作者身份、环境成本和在线社群之间的碰撞。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Blockchain, NFTs, and digital ownership debates because it turned a technical ownership mechanism into a mainstream art-market event.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“区块链、NFT 与数字所有权争论”阶段，因为它把一种技术性所有权机制转化为主流艺术市场事件。
events.connectionHint: It connects to crypto markets, digital scarcity, platform speculation, artist monetization, and later skepticism after NFT prices fell.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到加密市场、数字稀缺性、平台投机、艺术家变现，以及 NFT 价格下跌后的怀疑。
sourceNotes: The 2021 Christie's sale is the canonical NFT art market milestone.
events.imageCaption: Everydays became the emblem of NFT art's sudden entry into mainstream auction culture.
events.imageCaptionZh: 《Everydays》成为 NFT 艺术突然进入主流拍卖文化的象征。

events.title: DALL-E 2 opens wider public access
events.titleZh: DALL-E 2 扩大公众访问
events.summary: DALL-E 2 made text-to-image generation visible to a broad public and sharpened debates over authorship, training data, labor, and visual culture.
events.summaryZh: DALL-E 2 让文本生成图像进入更广泛公众视野，并加剧关于作者身份、训练数据、劳动和视觉文化的争论。
events.eventIntro: In 2022, DALL-E 2 became one of the systems that introduced many non-specialists to high-quality text-to-image generation. Users could describe an image in words and receive synthetic visual outputs in seconds.
events.eventIntroZh: 2022 年，DALL-E 2 成为让许多非专业用户第一次接触高质量文本生成图像的系统之一。用户可以用文字描述图像，并在几秒内获得合成视觉结果。
events.whyMatters: The event mattered because image generation stopped feeling like a laboratory demonstration and became an interface. Artists, designers, educators, publishers, and platforms had to confront how visual production changes when language becomes a control surface.
events.whyMattersZh: 这个事件重要，因为图像生成不再像实验室演示，而变成界面。艺术家、设计师、教育者、出版者和平台不得不面对：当语言成为控制界面时，视觉生产如何变化。
events.phaseRelation: It belongs to Generative AI and synthetic image culture because prompts, datasets, model behavior, and authorship became central artistic and social questions.
events.phaseRelationZh: 它属于“生成式 AI 与合成图像文化”阶段，因为提示词、数据集、模型行为和作者身份成为核心艺术与社会问题。
events.connectionHint: It connects to AI / Machine Learning, copyright disputes, design work, stock imagery, misinformation, and the longer history of software-assisted image editing.
events.connectionHintZh: 它连接到 AI / 机器学习、版权争议、设计劳动、图库图像、虚假信息，以及软件辅助图像编辑的更长历史。
sourceNotes: DALL-E 2 is a widely cited public milestone in text-to-image generative AI.
events.imageCaption: DALL-E 2 made text-to-image generation legible as a public creative interface.
events.imageCaptionZh: DALL-E 2 让文本生成图像作为公共创作界面变得可见。
